gumtree_entries.description: ADDED i2: A '%' escape character that is not followed by two hex digits (here it is the very last byte) is an invalid encoding, so decoding must fail.
ADDED i4: A null "always encode" array is allowed; the constructor simply succeeds.
ADDED i5: Characters that must always be encoded are stored in a BitSet keyed by the byte value, so a negative byte is rejected by the constructor.
ADDED i7: encode(Object) only accepts byte arrays; any other type triggers an exception.
ADDED i9: encode(Object) returns null when given a null object.
ADDED i10: encode(byte[]) returns null when given a null array.
ADDED i11: Encoding the single byte 0 (configured as an always-encode char) yields "%00"; encoding that result again percent-encodes the leading '%' to "%2500".
ADDED i13: decode(Object) returns null when given a null object.
ADDED i14: decode(Object) only accepts byte arrays; any other type triggers an exception.
ADDED i16: With plusForSpace enabled, decoding a '+' (byte 43) yields a space (byte 32).
ADDED i17: Bytes that need no decoding pass through unchanged.
ADDED i18: Encoding a byte and then decoding the result reproduces the original byte.
ADDED i19: byte 0 encodes to "%00"
ADDED i20: decode(byte[]) returns null when given a null array.
ADDED i21: With plusForSpace enabled, a space (byte 32) is encoded as '+' (byte 43) while the remaining bytes are left untouched.
ADDED i22: When nothing needs encoding, encode returns the very same array instance.
ADDED i23: encode(Object) returns the same byte[] instance when no byte needs encoding.
ADDED i24: The default codec percent-encodes non-ASCII bytes: byte -59 (0xC5) becomes "%C5".
ADDED i25: "%C5"
ADDED i26: encode(Object) followed by decode(Object) yields a new (non-same) byte[] result.
